newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares open bourse trade slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: German shares open bourse trade slightly higher.

text.p: German shares were slightly higher in bourse trade on Tuesday, boosted by an overnight rally on Wall Street, but uncertainty ahead of a possible interest rate rise in the U.S. limits turnover early on.
Market players expected Chairman of the U.S. Federal Reserve Alan Greenspan to announce a 25 basis-point rise in key U.S. interest rates after the Federal Open Market Committee meeting today.
The DAX index of 30 German blue-chip shares stood at 3,332.96 points, up 11.12 points or 0.33 percent early on.
"We expect an interest rate hike today, so we're waiting around until then," a Frankfurt trader said.

Shares in German builder Hochtief AG advanced strongly in bourse trade on Tuesday, lifted by an announcement that it and Deutsche Bank AG would later in the day release details of a "share pool" in Philipp Holzmann AG, Germany's largest builder.

Hochtief was up 1.10 marks, 1.5 percent, at 72.50 marks as it and Holzmann were expected to announce a deal giving Hochtief increased control over its industry rival, while attempting to sidestep cartel office objections to it increasing its existing stake in Holzmann.
The two firms said they would inform the media at 1100 GMT about plans to pool stakes totalling almost 50 percent held in Holzmann by Deutsche and Hochtief.
Shares in Thyssen AG and Krupp-Hoesch AG were both lower in pre-bourse trade on Tuesday after the two companies announced late on Monday that Krupp was calling off its takeover bid for Thyssen.

The two companies said on Monday after five days of talks they were planning to set up a joint steel venture and explore other areas of cooperation. Thyssen was down nearly ten percent early on, while Krupp lost 7.24 percent in early bourse.
Thyssen was down 41.50 marks, or 9.94 percent, at 376 marks, while Krupp was down 24.50 marks, or 7.24 percent, at 314 marks.
Merck KGaA was up 3.34 percent at 68 marks after it announced an increase in group net profits from 368 marks to 502 marks.
